sections.description: Uses examples to show how deliberate processes prevent customers from feeling abandoned when staff changes occur. Highlights Edward Jones's practice of shadowing a senior advisor for a year and handing over cases to the successor, with compensation design to support the transition.
sections.title: Continuity of relationships: handoffs, rewards, and trust

sections.description: Recounts Land's End's 1983 experience in Dodgeville, WI, including a 98.6% shipping guarantee and the idea of imagining customers’ lives (e.g., UPS driver experience, trying on a turtleneck) as a measure of reliability. Frames reliability as a holistic customer experience.
sections.title: Lifetime reliability through customer-centered experiences (Land's End case)

summary: Jeanne Bliss argues that reliable customer relationships are built by designating simple, observable 'service magnets'—experiential touches that position you as a knowledge resource and partner—rather than pushing constant sales. She cites concrete examples: a penny-arcade-like magnet in TD Bank stores that attracts families and enables rapid onboarding, a deliberate staff-handoff process at Edward Jones to prevent customers from feeling forgotten, and Land's End’s life-centered reliability, including a guarantee and a focus on imagining customers’ daily experiences. Across these cases, the thread is clear: think about customers on their terms, maintain continuity when personnel change, and make reliability a visible, ongoing commitment rather than a transactional promise.
title: Decide to Be There for Your Customers: Building Reliability Through Service Magnets and Thoughtful Handoffs
topics: risk of losing customers after staff change
